newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia T-bill yields at record low on easy rouble.
newsitem.headline: Russia T-bill yields at record low on easy rouble.

text.p: The Russian government paper market saw record high turnover and low yields following a heavy rouble inflow from the interbank market and the absence of other investment possibilities, dealers said on Thursday.
*Average yield fell to 26.1 pct from 28.2 pct on Tuesday, the previous trading day
*Turnover rose to 8.54 trln rbls from 5.18 trln rbls
*The Central Bank sold 534 bln rbls of series 23006, 23005, 24011 and 24012 bills and bonds
*Banks transferred 4.49 trln rbls to their accounts on the government securities trading system before the market opened
"T-bill yields reached historically low levels and the possibility of a further fall is much stronger than of a price rise," Troika Dialog head of fixed income Robert Devane said.
Dealers said yields on short-term paper dipped below 20 percent, falling to overnight credit rate levels.
Yields on medium-term paper fell to 21-23 percent, Russian operators focused on OFZ interest-bearing bonds.

"The volumes in the 24011 and 24012 issues were very big, as investment to the next coupon payment into the issues give a reasonable yield even after taxes -- somewhere around 30-32 percent," Bank Rossiisky Kredit dealer Konstantin Svyatny said. "Now it is a real alternative to medium-term T-bills."
